speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about transport allowances for NSmen who stay out during their ICT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We must recognise that NS is a contribution and sacrifice to the nation, but we also gain from the experience in many intangible ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our approach, therefore, is a more general one, to provide an allowance or Service Pay to support the basic personal upkeep of NSFs and NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We regularly review NS allowances to ensure that they remain appropriate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The last review was in December 2015 when it was adjusted upwards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Amrin Amin asked how MINDEF prepares our NSFs for life after NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is an important question because learning new skills is one major aspect of NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These could be vocational skills, such as driving, maintenance or physical training as an instructor, or soft skills, such as leadership and teamwork.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we can go further by formally accrediting the skills that are learnt in NS which NSmen can use for their future careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MINDEF has been working with SkillsFuture Singapore under the Ministry of Education (MOE) on this initiative.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, the teamwork we learn in NS, I think, is far better than many of the commercial workshops.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Throughout their full-time NS, they could also be accredited with other competencies, such as leadership, technical or specialist skills.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These achievements will be reflected in the enhanced Certificate of Service given to NSFs on their Operationally Ready Date.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By 2018, the Certificate will be made more comprehensive to include additional achievements, such as awards, commendations and milestones, that an NSF acquires during their service, their full-time NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: While accrediting skills learnt in NS is a useful enhancement of the NS experience, this is neither the main objective nor the key takeaway of NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: NS fulfils the obligation and accords the honour of contributing to the defence of our country.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The lasting benefits are the development of character and resilience, and the camaraderie and friendships forged with fellow NSmen.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ultimately, the fact that someone has completed NS well demonstrates his commitment and dedication, especially in a challenging unit that stretches his abilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This should speak for itself and be valued and recognised by the whole society, including employers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, more than one million Singaporeans have gone through the rite of passage of NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about the continued importance of NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Other countries, such as France and Sweden, have abolished conscription since the end of the Cold War.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Yet, in today's increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment, these countries are considering reinstating conscription.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, it was just reported in the media yesterday that Sweden has already decided to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We should learn from these examples and cherish the institution of NS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Recently, I read an article in the New York Times written by Karl Marlantes, a US Marine Corps veteran of the Vietnam War.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Marlantes highlights the importance of the US draft.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The draft gave all eligible American men a shared experience fighting for their country, socialised Americans of all backgrounds to the idea that they are all equally American.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: After the war, the US military abandoned the draft and transitioned to an all-volunteer force.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This, Marlantes argues, deprived Americans of the common experience and undermined the American social fabric, which has manifested itself in divisive politics today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Indeed, as Dr Goh Keng Swee said in 1967, and I quote, "Nothing creates loyalty and national consciousness more speedily and more thoroughly than participation in defence and membership of the armed forces.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: NS is a core part of the Singaporean identity, not just for males, but for mothers, wives, daughters and girlfriends who supported and encouraged our NSmen in their contribution and sacrifice.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It builds mutual trust within society, and between society and the Government.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our NS50 tagline "From My Generation to Yours" anchors the theme that NS is a shared responsibility and remains crucial to Singapore's security and nation-building.

speaker: The Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The NS system we have today is something we can be collectively proud of and continue to build on in the next 50 years and beyond.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our principle of embracing different cultures and faiths while building a shared Singaporean identity has been the foundation of our success and will continue to be so in the years to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But it must never be taken for granted, as evidenced by our own early history of religious tensions and race riots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a small country, we remain vulnerable to pressures from around the world and at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The pressures will only increase in the face of hybrid warfare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Amrin Amin and Ms Low Yen Ling asked about the threat that hybrid warfare poses to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Attackers will continue to devise ways to exploit our growing reliance on technology across all sectors of society, targeting all pillars of our Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Ng has earlier spoken about the ongoing threat of cyberattacks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But as history has shown, they are clearly effective in targeting all sectors of society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The devastating Maria Hertogh riots in 1950 arose out of newspaper reports that gave competing versions of the facts about legal proceedings and Maria's stay in the convent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These were distortions of facts by the media that was used as a tool of Muslim activism against colonialists.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And this took place in an age when news was spread in print or simply by word of mouth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Information attacks today are far more effective and dangerous, when technology permeates every aspect of our lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The spread of fake news and misinformation is much accelerated with WhatsApp and Facebook, and its impact is amplified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It was a distortion of facts, again aimed at inciting hostility among different groups in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It went viral and could have led to a breakdown in our society, similar to the Maria Hertogh riots but with far greater impact, if not for discerning netizens who reported the "insensitive article".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It clearly showed that we must act to protect the bonds that hold us together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Low Yen Ling, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Amrin Amin asked how we can respond to new hybrid threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Now in its 33rd year, Total Defence remains our best defence and response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The avenue of threats is new ‒ social media, the Internet and electronic devices, but the threats are the same ‒ distortions and falsehoods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And they target the same vulnerabilities ‒ our differences in race, religion and background.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, to deal with our new challenges, the way we practise Total Defence has to evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And we may find the social and psychological pillars of Total Defence gaining more prominence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the cyber domain, each individual is the first line of defence by guarding against phishing and hacking attempts through simple actions, such as using strong passwords for our personal devices and online accounts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Businesses also play an important role by putting in place necessary cybersecurity measures and training their staff to respond to potential risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The latest threat hijacks Internet of Things devices like security cameras and media players that you might have in your own home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Securing these devices, as well as your phones and laptops is, therefore, the first step in cyber defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the area of fake news, again, each individual is the first line of defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We need to be discerning and responsible with what we read and decide to share online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When you see a shocking article, for example, a good first step is to Google it and see if it is being reported on reputable news sites like the British Broadcasting Corporation, Reuters or Channel NewsAsia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: If you find fake news, it could be as simple as reporting a post to Facebook or commenting to expose the falsehood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is a movement in Eastern Europe called the Baltic Elves that does just that ‒ fighting trolls and disinformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am glad that Singaporeans are also stepping up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, when a Whatsapp message was circulating in December last year, warning of potential terrorist attacks in popular shopping areas, many citizens countered by warning that the message was unsubstantiated and should not be circulated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Singaporeans must have confidence in our own community and institutions and be discerning enough to question, check and push back against fake news, instead of simply forwarding it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is even more so when fake and distorted news have an impact on our security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is even more so, given the security challenges we face in the ideological battle with terrorist groups like ISIS in social media.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It has also released several propaganda videos and magazines in Bahasa Malay that are targeted at Muslims in the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These are aimed at inciting hostility and violence against other groups in our society that do not fall within ISIS' definition of being Muslim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our youths who are active on social media are particularly vulnerable; it is not difficult to access videos of beheadings juxtaposed with those showing an idyllic society under ISIS and a fighter explaining why it is every Muslim's duty to join ISIS, followed by a celebration of his martyrdom in death.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our Mufti and Muslim groups, such as the Religious Rehabilitation Group (RRG), have made clear that ISIS' methods go against Islam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These Muslim groups have been reaching out to educate the community through counselling, publications and speeches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the individual level, when confronted with extremist material, instead of forwarding it, our first instinct should be to check with our Mufti and Islamic authority, Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura (MUIS), and then commenting to counter such views.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We should not allow exclusivist thinking to permeate the minds of our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must have the psychological resilience to resist and reject materials that we suspect are untrue, extremist or exclusivist, which may have a negative impact on our social cohesion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Dr Teo Ho Pin and Mr Lee Yi Shyan rightly noted that Total Defence requires a whole-of-society effort and asked about MINDEF's Total Defence efforts and how we reach out and engage Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MINDEF will enhance our extensive partnerships across the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will collaborate closely across the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was an opportunity to remember our heritage and draw out messages of psychological and social defence and remind Singaporeans why we cannot rely on others to defend our home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are working with MHA in SGSecure to encourage Singaporeans to put Total Defence into action in the fight against terrorism, by building community vigilance, cohesion and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Within SAF, we are training our Servicemen to be prepared citizens and active responders, such as by equipping them with basic first aid and firefighting skills, so that they can support the civil pillar of Total Defence in their personal capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One such example was Military Expert 1 (ME1) Gregory Poh from the Republic of Singapore Air Force 113 Squadron.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In November 2016, ME1 Poh was on his way home from work when he noticed that a child at the playground was having seizures and was not breathing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He administered cardiopulmonary resuscitation immediately, continued to keep the child's condition stable and assisted the paramedics when they arrived.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Members can pick up a set and try out for yourselves from the library later on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This game, an example of a ground-up initiative, was designed by Mr Wan Junyan, an SGfuture participant, who was inspired by discussions with students on how to convey Total Defence lessons in a more engaging manner and developed in collaboration with MOE and MHA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It educates youths on how society can come together to better prepare for terrorist threats based on real-life examples, respond to them and recover from them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that through the game, our youths will grow to become Total Defence advocates amongst their peers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our younger generation will shape the future of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to ensure that they have the same commitment to Total Defence and the right instincts to face future threats and challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MINDEF is, therefore, working with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth's Committee on Citizen Engagement and partners like the National Youth Council to engage youths in conversations on what it takes to build up Singapore's psychological defence from their perspectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I hope there will be many more youths like Nurul Fatimah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She was a 14-year-old student in a local madrasah when she decided to attend CampTeen, which encourages cross-cultural friendships amongst students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She says, "For nine years of my life, I lived thinking that it was best to just stay within my comfort zone, without thinking of the importance of mixing around in this multicultural land.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Now, I know that common space is really significant to our generation today, but the bonds are not easily made." Now 17, and inspired by her experience, she is an active youth advocate with OnePeople.sg, which runs CampTeen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will engage economic and community leaders through ACCORD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked for an update on the implementation of the ACCORD proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, under the "We Support YOU in NS" initiative, the ACCORD Family and Community Council has been encouraging merchants and retailers to show their support for NSmen by offering discounts and benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Cheng Eng Wah, iDental's founder and Principal Dental Surgeon, readily agreed to have promotions on metal braces for NSFs when his team raised this initiative to him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Alluding to a Chinese saying 有 国 才 有 家, Dr Cheng explained: "There is no home without a nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I believe we need a strong army to punch above our weight." And he is not alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ACCORD members have also helped us to reach out to new citizens and Permanent Residents who will become an integral part of our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Alumni from these schools who have been through NS also returned to share their experiences and communicate the importance of NS for Singapore's defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we will reach out to individuals directly, because they can be empowered to initiate their own Total Defence efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Priya Shahane, Chief Human Resources officer of AXA Singapore, introduced a system to plan for coverage of duties in advance when an employee is called up for ICT in her company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This allowed AXA employees like Mr Pan Chee Keong, an Assistant Manager, to go for ICT without worrying about work piling up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We saw this when a 40-metre tall and 6.5-metre wide Tembusu tree toppled at the Singapore Botanic Gardens last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At least a hundred of those present rushed forward to push the branches and logs away to help those who were under the tree when it fell.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The future may be uncertain, the threats more unpredictable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will stand together with resilience and confidence, just as we have done before, ride out any crisis and emerge stronger as one people.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarifications.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: This is an organisation being created almost	de novo.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Are there any other models for us to follow or are we just pioneering this on our own?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: If we are pioneering this on our own, then it is going to start in about a year's time.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Do we have the capabilities within our existing people to do that?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: If not, how would we be developing this, because this is quite ground-breaking?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: You would remember in 2013, we announced the set-up of the Cyber Defence Operations Hub.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Obviously, with many of our systems being dependent on computer systems, data linkages and, particularly for all militaries and especially for the Singapore military because we are leveraging technology, we recognise that our strength can be exploited as a weakness.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I have gone to France to look at them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: They have a fairly well-developed system and there are different organisational structures, not only for the military but actually, more importantly, how the military coordinates as part of a national cyber defence.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: About this SAFTI new training area revamp, I think it is a great idea and overdue.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: At the same time, I would like to ask the Minister if he would consider two points.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: One is when we move the grounds and put up new buildings and all that, that we do not lose the history and the old names that were used in the old training grounds.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
text: We will do us a big disservice if Peng Kang Hill is changed to another name.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We want some resonance, and it is across the system and across all our agencies.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: Even as we update ourselves, refresh our systems to meet new needs, we want to retain a sense of history that can carry across generations.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, I will put that to SAF and leave it to them how they will do it.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I do not think they will be physically removing some hills or features, but even if they do, they can convert hills to street names, I suppose, but I will leave it to them.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The Member's second point is a significant one on safety.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is much easier and, just like buildings, to design safety in.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I learnt that when I was the Manpower Minister and had to deal with injuries and deaths at the workplace.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: For example, they said some buildings are designed and are beautiful but very hard to clean.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: It is much easier to design safety in across not only just the building but the lifetime maintenance of that building.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In this case, Mr Foo is saying, during your operations, can you design it, so that, for instance, your video feedback actually gives you an alert to say this is an unsafe zone?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: So, yes, that will be taken into consideration.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: We are very heartened to hear that NS, which we are celebrating our 50th Anniversary this year, a timeless institution, is still very strong.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I am particularly heartened to hear that the young men are very keen to do combat vocations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I wish I could say the same for my generation but not sure it would be true.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But I am particularly heartened because, in my personal anecdotal experience, I know people coming up saying they want to join the Naval Diving Unit as well.
